title: m* read as worst-case, not per-instance: affirmative answer unsupported in informative regime

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap type:** definitional / faithfulness (F2) — the proof answers the *worst-case* reading of $m^*$, but the problem defines $m^*$ via the *observed unlabeled pairs*.

**Where:** `solution.tex`, Remark "On the reading of $m^*$", Proposition 6, and the final Conclusion.

**The issue.** The problem defines
$$m^*(\varepsilon,\delta,n) = \text{labeled complexity by restricting to disjunctions consistent with the unlabeled pairs and applying standard compatibility-based PAC bounds}.$$
This is the *per-instance* quantity
$$m^*_D = O\!\Big(\tfrac1\varepsilon\big(\mathrm{VCdim}(C(U))\ln\tfrac1\varepsilon+\ln\tfrac1\delta\big)\Big),\qquad C(U)=\{h\in C: h(a)=h(b)\ \forall (a,b)\in U\},$$
which genuinely depends on $D$ through $\mathrm{VCdim}(C(U))$. This is the standard Balcan–Blum compatibility framework, whose entire point is that unlabeled data can make $\mathrm{VCdim}(C(U)) \ll \mathrm{VCdim}(C)=\Theta(n)$.

The submission instead **reads $m^*$ as the worst case over compatible $D$**, getting $m^* = \Theta((n+\ln\frac1\delta)/\varepsilon)$, and then matches it with plain supervised disjunction learning (literal elimination), using **no unlabeled pairs**. The submission explicitly notes (and dismisses as "vacuous") the per-$D$ reading where $\mathrm{VCdim}(C(U))=0$ gives $m^*_D=\Theta(\ln(1/\delta)/\varepsilon)$ — a baseline with NO $n$-dependence.

**Why this is a real gap, not style.** On such a $D$ (e.g. all pairs forcing the version space to a single hypothesis), the submitted algorithm uses
$m=\Theta\big(\tfrac{n}{\varepsilon}\ln\tfrac1\varepsilon\big)$ labels, while $m^*_D=\Theta(\ln(1/\delta)/\varepsilon)$. Since $n$ can grow independently of $\varepsilon,\delta$, we have $m = \omega(\mathrm{poly}(m^*_D))$: the label count is **not** $\mathrm{poly}(m^*_D)$. Thus the algorithm fails the requirement precisely in the regime where unlabeled data is informative — the only nontrivial regime. Proposition 6's claim $m=O(m^*\ln(1/\varepsilon))$ holds only against worst-case $m^*$; against $m^*_D$ the ratio is unbounded ($\sim n$).

**What must be fixed.** Either (a) give a rigorous, sourced argument that the problem really intends the worst-case reading (hard to sustain given the "consistent with the unlabeled pairs" phrasing), or (b) replace the algorithm with one that *uses* the unlabeled pairs and provably spends $\mathrm{poly}(m^*_D)$ labels on every compatible $D$ — including those with small $\mathrm{VCdim}(C(U))$. The current "no unlabeled pairs at all" design structurally cannot adapt to $\mathrm{VCdim}(C(U))$.
